name: Splice Machine
tagline: Hadoop-era ACID SQL database running OLTP on HBase and analytics on Spark; vendor insolvent since 2021.
description: Splice Machine put an ANSI SQL, ACID relational database on top of the Hadoop stack. It reused Apache Derby's parser and optimizer, executed short transactional queries directly against HBase regions and pushed large analytical plans to Spark, which gave HTAP on a single Hadoop cluster with MVCC snapshot isolation. The engine was published on GitHub under AGPLv3 next to a commercial edition, and the company later marketed itself around machine learning. It entered insolvency proceedings in July 2021 and the repository went quiet the same month, so it now matters only to teams still running it.
statusNote: The company entered insolvency proceedings in July 2021 and the open-source repo has been idle since. Consider CockroachDB, YugabyteDB or TiDB for scale-out SQL.
basedOn: Apache HBase, Apache Spark and Apache Derby

pricing.notes: The AGPL edition remains on GitHub; commercial support ended with the company.

scale.notes: Scales with the underlying HBase/HDFS and Spark clusters.

strengths: Full ACID SQL with joins and secondary indexes on top of HBase, which HBase alone lacks
Dual execution: HBase for point operations, Spark for large analytical queries
Derby-derived SQL front end with Java stored procedures and triggers
weaknesses: Vendor insolvent since 2021; no maintained releases or support
Requires running a full Hadoop, HBase and Spark stack
AGPL license on the open-source edition
